posts.title: Summer festival dates
posts.excerpt: Two shrine nights and a riverside stage. Beginners welcome on the last piece.
posts.content:
We play the Hibiki shrine festival on the last Saturday of July and the lantern night in mid-August.

In September the whole school plays the riverside stage. Rehearsals start in June.

posts.title: Our new oak sticks
posts.excerpt: A local carpenter turned forty pairs from one fallen tree.
posts.content:
The oak fell by the shrine in last year’s typhoon. The carpenter dried it for a year before cutting.

They are heavier than our old sticks. Expect sore forearms for a week, then a deeper sound.

posts.title: Why we practise on old tyres
posts.excerpt: Half of every class starts on rubber, not cowhide. Here is why.
posts.content:
A tyre does not ring, so you hear only your hands. Uneven strokes show at once, and nobody minds the noise.

It also saves the drumheads, which cost more than a month of classes to replace.
